sources.title: Security Incident Report 16th July
limitations: Does not identify the selected drain transaction in its text.
Statement that finite approvals were unaffected describes this incident's affected population; it is not a general proof that finite allowances cannot be drained.
sources.notes: The protocol attributes the incident to a new facet missing validation around arbitrary external calls. It links the affected facet at 0xf28a352377663ca134bd27b582b1a9a4dad7e534.

sources.title: Illicit Fund Flow Case Study: LI.FI Attack
supports: Explicitly links the selected 0xd82f...3873 transaction as an attack example
Identifies the incident actor and LI.FI diamond
sources.notes: The article distinguishes attack transactions from later swaps and laundering. Only the attack example is a candidate here.

sources.title: Socket Tech Incident Analysis
supports: Prior approvals were consumed by arbitrary transferFrom calls
limitations: Selected drain hash is independently checked through RPC, not directly linked as a transaction in the reviewed article.
One attack-contract anchor has inconsistent visible label/address; do not use that abbreviated anchor as transaction identity evidence.
sources.notes: The receipt matches the named actor, gateway emitter, and 127 nonzero USDC transfer sources. Trace-based attribution is still an admission requirement.

sources.title: USDC Permit Phishing Drain
sources.displayedDateMeaning: Incident-date header; actual publication timestamp was not independently established and must not be used as a historical intelligence cutoff.
supports: Exact transaction hash, chain, block, actor and reported permit-drain flow
Selected victim and max-uint256 Approval fields
limitations: Phishing page, social engineering, and EIP-7702 Poisoner attribution are source claims not independently established by the captured receipt.
The page banner says Flash Loan while its body says no flash loan; that category is excluded from our labels.
An original wallet prompt and signed typed-data request are not supplied.
sources.notes: The source describes a permit redemption followed by three USDC transfers. The RPC receipt independently confirms one maximum Approval event and three Transfer events, but does not itself prove phishing intent or the call mechanism.

sources.title: CertiKAlert incident alert linked by a secondary incident index
sources.notes: Link discovered through an incident index. Do not treat an unread alert as corroboration.

sources.title: ERC-20: Token Standard
sources.notes: Approval and Transfer event semantics inform decoding; they do not establish informed consent or maliciousness.
